cases.letter:
To: the District Department of Transportation (DDOT)
Subject: Request for safety study at 23rd Street NW & L Street NW

Dear colleagues at DDOT,

We write to ask for a safety study at 23rd Street Northwest & L Street Northwest, and for treatment on the roads you own: 23rd Street Northwest, L Street Northwest, New Hampshire Avenue Northwest, and Washington Circle Northwest.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 50 crashes, 8 of them with injuries. One pedestrian and 2 cyclists were injured. One person was killed. Records count injured by mode as cyclist, motorist, and pedestrian and killed by mode as cyclist, motorist, and pedestrian. This location is a city priority location under the city's high injury network. The latest recorded safety project is Local Sidewalk Restoration Citywide Maintenance (2032). Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the yearly cost of harm is $0.5 million.

We note this earlier program was tried here: This corner got Leading Pedestrian Interval signals in 2019. The earlier program's effect was not shown — across the city at 267 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes could be zero. Please take a different approach rather than repeating it here.

We ask you to assess:

* Reflective backplates on the traffic signals. Federal name: Backplates with Retroreflective Borders. This is expected to avoid about 0.2 injury crashes per year, equal to about $82,000 in harm avoided per year in DOT values, and would pay for itself if kept under $0.6 million. Evidence needs a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

* Longer yellow signal times. Federal name: Yellow Change Intervals. This is expected to avoid about 0.1 injury crashes per year, equal to about $43,000 in harm avoided per year, and would pay for itself if kept under $0.3 million. Evidence needs a site check for an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.

Please study the junction and confirm what is feasible and needed on site.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

Subject: Request for safety study and signal fixes at East 57th Street & 2nd Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We write about the junction of East 57th Street & 2nd Avenue.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 181 crashes, including 98 injury crashes. Among those hurt were 33 pedestrians and 38 cyclists. Using the U.S. DOT's official values, the yearly cost of harm at this junction is $6.7 million a year. The location is a city priority location. We ask you to carry out a safety study for the junction on the roads you are responsible for, and to consider the following fixes where a site check shows they fit:
